settings.advancedModeHint: Show test advanced settings, raw status values, and the diagnostics tab
settings.closeToTray: Minimize to tray when closing the window (instead of quitting)
settings.pollHint: Shorter interval applies rules faster at slightly higher CPU cost.
settings.showAdvanced: Show advanced priorities (I/O / Memory) in the rule editor
settings.highPrecisionTimerHint: Requests 0.5 ms timer resolution via ntdll. Note: since Windows 10 2004, the request is per-process — only PaceDock's own timers are guaranteed; whether the global tick is raised is decided by the system. Global effect requires the registry value GlobalTimerResolutionRequests=1 (this app never writes it).
settings.updateConfirmBody: PaceDock {version} will be installed. Current version: {current}. Continue?

timer.detectHint: Reads the currently effective system-wide timer resolution (the same three values as Clockres). Not refreshed automatically.
timer.stateOn: Request active — PaceDock holds a 0.5 ms request.
timer.range: Supported range: finest {min} ms – coarsest {max} ms (same values as Clockres)
timer.globalNote: This reflects PaceDock only. To give the whole system (including games) 0.5 ms, enable Global mode below.
timer.globalHint: Writes GlobalTimerResolutionRequests=1, restoring pre-Win10-2004 global semantics: PaceDock's 0.5 ms request lifts the whole system tick (games included). The value is only a policy gate — the tick falls back automatically when this app closes; delete the value to fully revert.
timer.globalReboot: Written — takes effect after a reboot.
timer.exemptHint: Windows 11 throttles backgrounded/occluded processes' timer resolution back to 15.6 ms. Games on the list are exempt: their 0.5 ms survives alt-tab or occlusion. The list persists — exemptions are re-applied automatically when a game restarts (new PID) and after PaceDock restarts; PaceDock reverts all exemptions on exit.
timer.exemptNone: The list is empty. Add a game and PaceDock will lift timer throttling whenever it runs.
timer.exemptNote: The exemption only prevents throttling — it does not grant 0.5 ms by itself. The game must request its own resolution, or Global mode must be on.

quick.title: GPU tuning
quick.scope: Quick tests rank candidates in this synthetic workload only. They do not establish an advantage over the original Windows policy or a game FPS improvement.
quick.candidateHint: Each candidate includes every LP of its physical core. Hybrid CPUs offer P-cores only, including core 0.
quick.noCandidates: No eligible cores, or this processor group topology is unsupported.
quick.estimateHint: Includes calibration, startup and restart costs. Retries, window checks and system waits can extend the duration.
quick.chooseCandidates: Select a GPU and at least one core, and enter valid durations.
quick.gapHint: Retest score gaps ≤ 0.5% are marked close. This is a display heuristic, not FPS improvement or statistical significance.
quick.manualChoice: No winner is preselected. You may select either valid retested core and confirm to apply.
quick.legacy: Legacy single-LP records are view-only. They cannot be applied or expanded automatically to a whole core.
quick.keepWindow: Keep the test window visible. Wait for cleanup and restoration.
quick.startConfirm: Testing sets whole-core policies and restarts the GPU. The display may briefly go black. The pre-test policy is restored at the end.
quick.applyConfirm: Set the complete physical core and restart the GPU:
quick.restoreConfirm: Restore the complete original policy saved before the last application and restart the GPU.
quick.deleteConfirm: Permanently delete this history entry and its capture data?
quick.recovery: A GPU recovery journal is still pending. Tests and application are blocked. Restart the app to retry recovery.
quick.exitBlocked: A GPU operation is in progress. Cancel the test and wait for cleanup, application or restoration to finish before closing the window.
quick.msiConfirm: Enable Message Signaled Interrupts (MSISupported=1)? The display device will be restarted.
quick.msiRestoreConfirm: Restore the previous MSI setting? The display device will be restarted.

baseline.WithinThreshold: No meaningful improvement over the default policy
baseline.hint: Measured against the OS default policy under identical conditions (captured before and after the candidate runs). This does not affect apply eligibility.
baseline.none: No default-policy comparison recorded for this session.

measure.hint: Attaches PresentMon to a running game (ETW-based; no process handles of the game are opened). Play normally for a while, then compare 1% lows before and after tuning. Anti-cheat tools generally tolerate this, but safety cannot be guaranteed for every game.
measure.compareHint: Δ: FPS rows show relative difference (%); MAD / Spike / Frames rows show absolute difference. Game measurements must not be compared against synthetic benchmark sessions (different workload).
measure.deleteConfirm: Permanently delete this measurement and its raw data?
